key_insight: DrugHarness turns computational drug discovery into an adaptive agent system that can not only execute many scientific operations, but also learn new skills from its own trajectories and feedback. This makes the harness evolvable as evidence and constraints change.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the difficulty of building AI agents for drug discovery that can reliably compose complex scientific workflows, preserve relationships between candidates and results, and adapt to shifting experimental evidence or task constraints.
method: Builds a modular agent harness with more than 80 scientific operations plus biomedical resources and task-specific code.
Preserves associations among candidates, results, and artifacts so execution history remains traceable and reusable.
Uses execution trajectories and outcome feedback to induce conditional skills, enabling the agent to evolve over time.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this offers a practical framework for creating more robust scientific agents that can manage complex, stateful workflows. It is especially relevant for domains like drug discovery where adaptability, traceability, and tool composition are critical.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing agent input -> scientific operations -> candidate/results/artifacts -> feedback -> skill induction
Icon grid for the 80+ scientific operations and biomedical resources
Feedback loop illustration highlighting conditional skill learning over multiple runs
State-tracking schematic showing how candidates, results, and artifacts stay linked
paper_title: DrugHarness: An Evolvable Agent Harness for Computational Drug Discovery
paper_authors: Yuxing Chen, Zhisheng Zhang, Cheng Tang, Wei Li, Minghui Zhang
